Injected journal failure rolls back publication head update and inserted version.

limitations: These eight tests exercise the application service directly against the real local PostgreSQL runtime. Synthetic fixture setup uses direct SQL and is not evidence of an end-user creation workflow.

The deliberately injected failing journal callback proves transaction rollback when audit publication fails. It is not a mock production audit pass. Real production audit/outbox and HTTP idempotency behavior require the separate API integration suite.

Model APIs, browser/UI behavior, migration execution, inheritance, relation definitions, advanced policy constraints, all import/workflow/MCP ingress adapters and release qualification are not qualified by this report.
Publication preserves explicit existing asset-version pins. Destructive changes remain blocked; no declarative migration or AT-MOD-01 migration-recovery pass is claimed.
Authorization is rechecked after waiting for canonical locks. Full enterprise concurrency/revocation/load qualification remains open.
The synchronous profile is bounded to 100 listable models, 1000 bound assets, 512 KiB combined cohort attribute JSON, 100000 combined validation nodes and 1000 nested validation issues.
Synthetic fixtures remain in the local development database. No immutable audit/version history was deleted to clean up test data.

Tenant ledger locking serializes model mutations and complete previews with other participating tenant mutations. Throughput and enterprise concurrency qualification remain open; this report does not establish a throughput target.
